shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Trading 1×A for 1×B changes my inventory from balanced (1,1,1) to less varied (0 A, 1 C, 2 B). Since I value goods equally and prefer variety, this reduces my utility.
I currently have equal amounts of A, B, and C. Trading 1 B for 1 A would reduce variety by leaving me with more A and no B, which lowers my utility.

Starting from a balanced bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 A changes my inventory from (A:1, C:1, B:1) to (A:3, C:1, B:0). Since I value variety and would lose all of B while creating a large imbalance, this reduces my utility despite gaining total quantity.
Trading 1×C for 1×B would change my balanced inventory from A:1, B:1, C:1 to A:1, B:2, C:0, reducing variety, which lowers my utility.
I currently hold A:1, B:1, C:1, so my bundle is perfectly balanced. Trading 1×B for 1×C would make it less varied (A:1, B:0, C:2), which lowers utility for my variety preference.

Starting from an even 1/1/1 bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 C leaves me with A:1, B:0, C:3. Since all goods are valued equally and extra units of a good I already have more of are less useful than maintaining variety, this trade reduces variety and lowers my utility.
Starting from one of each good, trading 1×A for 1×B would leave me with less variety and a more imbalanced bundle (A:0, C:1, B:2), which lowers my utility.
Starting from an even bundle (1 A, 1 B, 1 C), exchanging 1 B for 1 A would make my inventory less balanced (2 A, 0 B, 1 C). Since I value variety and all goods equally, this lowers my utility.

Starting from an even bundle of 1A, 1B, 1C, this trade changes my inventory to 3A, 0B, 1C. Since I prefer variety and value goods I have less of more highly, losing my only B and increasing an already sufficient good reduces variety and lowers my utility.
I currently have equal amounts of A, B, and C. Trading 1 C for 1 B would reduce variety by leaving me with no C and extra B, so it lowers my utility.
Trading 1×B for 1×C would leave me with A:1, B:0, C:2, reducing variety. Since I value goods equally and prefer a balanced bundle, this lowers my utility.

Starting from an even bundle (A1, B1, C1), giving 1 B and receiving 2 C increases my total goods and leaves me with A1, B0, C3. Although variety decreases somewhat, the gain of two units for one makes this trade beneficial overall.
Trading 1 A for 1 B would change my balanced inventory from A:1, B:1, C:1 to A:0, B:2, C:1, reducing variety. Since I value the goods equally and prefer a more even mix, this trade lowers my utility.
Trading 1 B for 1 A would change my balanced inventory from (A:1, B:1, C:1) to (A:2, B:0, C:1), reducing variety. B is also currently harder to obtain, so giving it up lowers my utility.
Giving up my only B would reduce variety, and B is currently harder to obtain. Although 2 A adds quantity, it makes my bundle less balanced overall.

Trading 1 C for 1 B changes my inventory from (A1, C1, B1) to (A1, C0, B2), which reduces variety. Since I value goods equally and prefer balanced holdings, this does not increase my utility. However, B is becoming harder to obtain, so receiving B may improve future bargaining power enough to justify the trade.

I currently have one of each good, so my bundle is perfectly balanced. Trading 1×B for 1×C would make my inventory less varied, and B is also becoming harder to obtain, increasing the opportunity cost of giving it up.
Giving up my only B for more C would reduce variety in my bundle. Since B is also becoming harder to obtain, this trade does not improve my utility.
Trading 1 A for 1 B improves my variety by adding a good I currently lack and reducing a good I have in higher quantity, which increases my utility.
I currently have no B, so gaining 1 B increases variety and is especially valuable. Giving 2 A reduces a surplus relative to B, leaving a more balanced bundle overall.
Trading 1 C for 1 B improves my variety: I currently have no B, so gaining B is more valuable than keeping an extra C. The new bundle is more balanced and increases my utility.
I currently have no B, so gaining 1 B greatly improves my variety. Giving 2 C reduces a surplus good, and the market update suggests B is especially valuable right now.

I value A, B, and C equally, but I prefer variety. Trading 1 A for 1 B would change my inventory from (A:1, B:1, C:1) to (A:0, B:2, C:1), which reduces variety and does not increase my utility. B may be scarcer in the market, but based on my own bundle this trade is not better for me.
